title: Deficiency in service claims against banks and insurers
p1:
A bank delays your transaction. An insurer rejects your genuine claim. Does that mean you have no option?

Many people assume large financial institutions cannot be questioned. But the law allows customers to raise complaints when services fall below expected standards.
p2:
A common misconception is that every disagreement with a bank or insurer is a deficiency in service. That is not true.

The issue is not simply an unfavorable decision. The problem arises when there is negligence, unreasonable delay, failure to provide promised services, or improper handling of a customer’s request.
p3:
For example, if an insurer delays processing a valid claim without a reasonable reason, or a bank fails to provide a committed service despite repeated requests, the customer may have grounds to complain.

The key takeaway: keeping records of applications, emails, receipts, and responses can make a major difference when proving poor service.
conclusion: Have you ever faced unnecessary delays or poor service from a bank or insurance company? What was your experience?
